title: docs/runbooks/agent-profile-operation.md never says how to choose a profile's max_tokens, which is the one non-obvious decision in authoring one
description:
Found while working LCLI-640 (2026-09-29). Filed rather than absorbed: the deliverable is a docs change, LCLI-640's is a profile.

The runbook is 126 lines and is the authoritative how-to for authoring and operating a profile. It documents the file format, discovery, validation, compilation, saved artifacts and rollback -- and says nothing about how to choose max_tokens. The field appears once, as the unexplained number 4000 in the step-1 example. Step 1's prose covers naming and references and stops there.

This is not a stylistic gap. Sizing is the only decision in a profile that has no obvious answer, and two separate efforts have now had to derive it by experiment rather than read it: OPAG-33 swept 10k-24k to set implementation 20000 / review 18000 / verification 16000, and LCLI-640 swept 8k-24k across four tasks to set documentation 20000. Whichever author comes next repeats that work from scratch, because the result lives in the .toml files rather than in the runbook.

The derivation is also NOT the obvious one, which is what makes writing it down worth more than the cost of the section. LCLI-640's thirteen-budget sweep measured that the omission curve is not monotone in max_tokens: on one task, 20000 selected 23 of 80 ranked blocks while 20500 selected 5, because context ranks COMPLETE blocks and a larger budget can admit one large high-scoring block whole, displacing several smaller ones. So the intuitive rule -- raise the budget until nothing more is dropped -- is wrong and can make a pack strictly worse. The working test OPAG-33 used (and LCLI-640 reused) is that no source scoring 9 or above may be fully omitted, read off the allowed-source catalog, with the sweep read as a table rather than as a curve that converges. LCLI-642 is the checking half of this -- it gates a profile whose declared sources cannot fit at all -- and is complementary, not a substitute: "it fits" and "the budget was chosen well" are different questions.

SCOPE, deliberately narrow: add a short section to docs/runbooks/agent-profile-operation.md on choosing max_tokens, carrying the sweep method, the >=9 test, the non-monotonicity warning and a pointer to the measurement. It should NOT restate LCLI-640's or OPAG-33's numbers as universal -- they are per-bundle measurements -- and it should NOT propose a change to lore's assembler, which would be a design question for the orchestrator.

acceptanceCriteria.text: docs/runbooks/agent-profile-operation.md explains how to choose a profile max_tokens, including the sweep method and the >=9 omission test, in the runbook section that already owns profile authoring
The section states that the omission curve is not monotone in the budget and that a larger budget can yield a strictly worse pack, so raising it until nothing more is dropped is not the rule
The section does not present any other bundle's budget as universal, and proposes no change to the pack assembler

plan: 1. Measure the sweep on this bundle myself (catalog via --json) and confirm the non-monotone pair before writing it down as fact.

2. Add the sizing section to docs/runbooks/agent-profile-operation.md after Step 1, naming the sweep method, the >=9 omission test, the non-monotonicity warning, and the agent-profile-capacity floor (LCLI-642 / DEC-11).
3. Gates solo: bun run lore check and bun test, plus lore validate on the edited file.
4. Tracker notes, ACs, complete; land via PR into dev.
implementationNotes: CROSS-REFERENCE TO ADD when this task writes the max_tokens section (recorded here so it is not lost, not as scope): LCLI-642 landed the `agent-profile-capacity` rule in `lore check` on 2026-09-29 (DEC-11). The runbook's sizing section should name the rule, because it is the enforcement half of exactly the decision this task documents: "which budget to choose" now has a floor that `lore check` reports -- the budget must hold the profile's complete declared set, and the finding names the declared size to raise it to. It ships warning-tier for one release, then as an error (LCLI-646). Note also that the four profiles in THIS repository were re-budgeted to hold their declared sets rather than narrowed (106000 / 62000 / 93000 / 62000), which makes them a worked example the section may cite -- with the caveat that they are per-bundle measurements and not universal numbers.

LCLI-644 IMPLEMENTED on branch docs/LCLI-644-max-tokens-sizing. Added an H2 section '## Choosing a max_tokens budget' to docs/runbooks/agent-profile-operation.md (after Steps, before Rollback) plus a one-sentence pointer in Step 1, at the line where max_tokens first appears in the example TOML. The section carries: the sweep method (3-4 representative tasks x a range of budgets, reading the pack's 'Allowed source catalog' or .data.catalog[] via --json), the >=9 omission test, the non-monotonicity warning, and the agent-profile-capacity floor (LCLI-642/DEC-11, warning now, error after LCLI-646).

MEASUREMENTS TAKEN IN THIS CHECKOUT for the section, rather than restating LCLI-640's: on the documentation profile, one task, the omission curve is non-monotone -- 19500 selected 20 sections and fully omitted 6 sources, 20000 selected 23 and omitted 5, 20500 selected just 5 and omitted 8. Mechanism read off the pack, not inferred: 'Release publishing > Steps > 3. Cut a release' is a single 13448-token section (score 8.428) that only fits at 20500, and admitting it consumes the room a dozen smaller sections were using. Omission is also task-dependent: at budget 20000 the same profile omitted 5, 4 and 1 sources across three different tasks, in different sets -- which is why the section says to judge across the swept tasks rather than one pack.

AC2 held deliberately: no budget is presented as universal (the only numbers are this bundle's, dated 2026-09-29 and framed as its own measurement), and the section states the non-monotonicity is correct ceiling behaviour rather than proposing any change to the assembler. The four .lore/agents/*.toml profiles are cited as a worked example of the method with the explicit caveat that their numbers are not defaults to copy; the raw numbers stay in the .toml files and on the completed LCLI-642 record, per the lesson that numbers in prose go stale.

lore sync also caught up docs/log.md (39 commit entries never logged since 6b92f002), carried in this PR deliberately: ADR-0007 defines log.md as a sync-time materialized artifact that lore check neither regenerates nor compares, so it is not gated either way and the catch-up is not a separate task.
finalSummary:
LCLI-644 delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#410 (branch docs/LCLI-644-max-tokens-sizing). docs/runbooks/agent-profile-operation.md gained a "Choosing a max_tokens budget" section: the sweep method, the >=9 omission test, the non-monotonicity warning (raise it until nothing more is dropped is not the rule), and the agent-profile-capacity floor from LCLI-642/DEC-11 -- plus a pointer from Step 1, where the field first appears. Its numbers were measured here rather than restated: on one task, budgets 19500/20000/20500 selected 20/23/5 sections and fully omitted 6/5/8 sources, because a single 13448-token section only fits at 20500; omission is task-dependent (5/4/1 sources across three different tasks at one budget). No budget is presented as universal, and no assembler change is proposed.

GATES, with versions named. bun 1.3.14, node v24.20.0. bun test exit 0: 4809 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail, 19758 expect() calls, 4810 tests across 134 files, 252.02s. bun run lore check exit 0: 82 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 9 out-of-bundle links skipped, "Agent profiles: 4 read, 0 over capacity". bun run lore validate on the edited file: ok, 0 errors, 0 warnings. The same-file anchor was proved in both directions: green on the clean tree, and a deliberately broken slug reddens lore check with broken-anchor at exit 6.

CI: run 36539450101 (pull_request) on the code head 526c9a8e -- success, 12 success / 1 skipped (promotion is manual, skipped by design on a dev PR), all five required dev contexts green. The tracker-only commits after it (this close) are covered by the merge gate on the final head. Also carried: the lore sync catch-up of docs/log.md (39 entries), a sync-time artifact ADR-0007 says lore check neither regenerates nor compares.
